Evidence level: PROVEN — documented by Florentine archives, banking records, and contemporary chronicles. Their patronage funded the Renaissance's greatest art.

title: Confucius Descendants (Kong Family)
description: The Kong family of Qufu claims direct patrilineal descent from Confucius (551-479 BCE), with a genealogy recognized in Chinese records for over two millennia — often called the world's longest documented family tree. Evidence level: DOCUMENTED-SCHOLARLY — the genealogy is recorded in official Chinese genealogical compilations, though the earliest centuries rely on traditional records modern scholars treat carefully. Kong descendants hold the hereditary title Duke Yansheng's successors.

title: Japanese Imperial Line

Emperor Naruhito is the 126th in the traditional count.

title: Charlemagne's Descendants
description: Charlemagne (742-814), crowned Emperor in 800, has documented descendants through his many children — but the famous claim that 'most Europeans descend from Charlemagne' rests on mathematics, not genealogy: with 40+ generations, anyone with European ancestry from that era is statistically likely to be an ancestor of millions. Evidence level: MIXED — the royal descents are PROVEN; the universal-descent claim is STATISTICAL reasoning, honestly labeled as such.

title: Bach Musical Family

Evidence level: PROVEN — documented by the Bach family's own genealogy (Ursprung der musicalisch-Bachischen Familie), church registers, and employment records. It is the classic case of transmitted craft.

title: How to Read Evidence Levels
description: Every record in this database carries an evidence level so readers can weigh claims honestly. PROVEN means contemporary documents and archives; DOCUMENTED-SCHOLARLY means scholarly consensus over compiled records; TRADITION means a community's own historical narrative, respected but distinct from archives; STATISTICAL means mathematical inference; WORD-OF-MOUTH means unverified oral or popular claims, included only when flagged as such. The ranking runs proven at the top to word-of-mouth at the bottom, and no record is ever promoted above its evidence.
